groups.label: Life rearranged round the dog
groups.note: Began as a summary of routines. Reworked once I saw how often the arranging went unseen until it stopped: the groomer's two hours, the bowl in the cupboard, the alarm at quarter past five.
groups.description: How the dog's needs come to order time, rooms and the share of care, often unnoticed until something interrupts them.

groups.label: A house on standby
groups.description: The dog as the presence that makes a house feel lived in, felt most sharply when the dog is out of it or gone.

groups.label: The dog between people
groups.note: Juno's account leads here, so I checked it was not hers alone. Rowan and Mabel both give the dog as a reason, and Mabel's talk to Pepper is the clearest case of the dog taking a place.
groups.description: The dog as a go-between: a reason others accept, a listener, and a way round the talk people find hard with each other.

groups.label: Easier than people
groups.description: The dog's love as simpler than people's, needing nothing to have been got right, and taking a place a person once held.

groups.label: The dog as a door, open or shut
groups.note: Mabel and Rowan pull in opposite directions. Kept as one theme because the contrast is the point: it turns on the dog and the place more than on the person.
groups.description: Whether a dog widens a life or narrows it turns on how far the dog can share the world outside the house. Pepper's ease takes Mabel out to the green, the classes and better care of herself. Skye's fear keeps Rowan in the flat and the dark hours. The bond is the same, the door is not.

groups.label: Love that keeps watch
groups.description: Care for the dog that is never free of vigilance: for its safety, for others' judgement, and for a future in which one of them is gone.
